name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Ruminococcus into several genera, of which Ruminococcus_F is one; the cited findings are about Ruminococcus in the broad sense.

sentences.text: Ruminococcus is a bacterial genus that is dominant in the human gut and whose species fall in the families Lachnospiraceae and Oscillospiraceae.

An analysis of more than 9,000 Ruminococcus metagenome-assembled genomes from over 5,000 subjects reported significant links between prevalence of species and subspecies and geographic origin, age, lifestyle and disease.

That study reported that Ruminococcus species from Lachnospiraceae encode carbohydrate-active enzymes potentially involved in metabolism of human N- and O-glycans, while those from Oscillospiraceae appeared more adapted to fiber metabolism.

A structural-proteomics study reported an expanded set of putative cellulosome-producing Ruminococcus species, including six previously unrecognized human symbionts; cellulosomes let anaerobic bacteria degrade recalcitrant plant polysaccharides.
